correctness.rationale: Two arc resistances in parallel give R=δ(L−δ)/L. The absolutely convergent Fourier identity for periodic h(u)=u²(1−u)² expresses R² as positive ∑(1−cos(2πmu))/m⁴; zero-sum quadratic form is strictly negative by Vandermonde invertibility of first n Fourier moments. Discrete cyclic second differences determine Gram eigenvalues b_j=(3−2sin²)/(4n sin⁴)>0, and sine/Chebyshev products yield pseudodeterminant and volume. Negative type is open above 2 on each finite set; consecutive-triple Hilbert triangle bound forces limiting exponent ≤2. Independent Fourier and Chebyshev values match n=3..16. The proof does not evaluate finite-n exact supremal p for n≥4.
